## fix-player2 — the player bugs still failing in play (input-driven repro first)

Branch s/fix-player2 (from master 75fbad4). Every fix has a headless NF_ISO test in
`crates/nf-view/tests/fix_player2_live.rs` that drives the real path (`nf_view::load` + `Sim::step_bond`)
and failed before its fix (all five shown failing on the pre-fix build, then green after).

**1. The grenade throw (weapon 0x35) — "press fire does nothing, then no weapon shoots."**
Root cause, two halves [M, decompile + audit fix-player2 claims 1-4]:
- The port spawned every round on the press tick. The game's throw is data: view state 9
  (`Player_SetFiringAnim` 0x1a3c70:52), the fire script queued, and the round spawns when the script's
  frame reaches `fire_anim_len` (+0x44 = 26 for 0x35 [L ee_start_07000001.bin]) with the +0x95C latch
  clear (`Player_SetWeaponAnimObj` case 9, 0x1a2e38:410-419); `fire_anim_len == 0` weapons spawn on the
  press tick (0x1a5460:688-693). The port's press-tick spawn fired a hitscan bullet with the grenade
  record instead of winding up.
- The refire timer: 0x35's fire_rate (+0x40) is 900 ticks [L]. `Player_SetWeaponAnimObj` case 4 zeroes
  BLData+0x92C when the draw finishes (0x1a2e38:316) — the port never reset it, so after the failed throw
  every weapon inherited the ~15 s timer. Also `Player_WeaponChange` (0x1a6f80:33-47) refuses all
  switching during view state 9 — ported as the fire-script gate in `Sim::step_bond`.
Fix (gun.rs + scene.rs): `Gun.fire_state`/`Gun.latch` (+0x95C semantics), `GunParams.fire_anim_len`,
the release-frame spawn, the fire-script-end → idle re-queue (case 9:449-456), the case-4 timer reset,
the state-9 switch block. The grenade itself spawns through `Bullet_init`'s contract: three spread draws
in the game's RNG order (0x12c5a0:166-184), speed +0x20, gravity via `+0x6C & 0x8`, silent spawn
(param_7 = 0xffff) — the throw sound is the fire script's op-1 command. *Deviations*: spawn origin is the
eye (the game uses midpoint(head, view-model bone 0) — no view bones in the port); the port's
`Grenade.range` doubles as the tick fuse, which the audit pinned to Bullet_init's hardcoded BU+0xFC =
210 (300 with +0x70 & 0x10000), NOT weapon_data+0x1C (0x35's is 5000.0 — the guard path in drone.rs
passes +0x1C into the same field and will explode late by fuse; out of this task's files, noted).
Test: `grenade_throw_spawns_at_the_release_frame_and_the_gun_recovers` + sisters (no hitscan on press,
idle script restored, P2K fires afterwards).

**2. Raptor drops unreliable.** The take-test log (`NF_PICKUPLOG=1`, in `Pickup::touches` + one env-gated
result line in `Drones::update_pickups` — the latter is the task's one minimal shared-file touch in
drone.rs) caught it live: a resting 07000001 guard drop (weapon 0xe) sits with its sphere centre ON the
floor (model centre y ≈ 0), so the take ray ends ON the floor triangle; the port's `segment` counts
t = 1.0 as a hit → `line_of_sight` false → the drop could never be taken. The game takes floor-resting
drops, so its `Collide_LineOfSight` (0x1edf50 → `Collide_RayIntersect` 0x1ec690) does not fail on the
endpoint contact. Fix (pickup.rs): the take test treats a hit at the ray's end (t ≥ 1 − 1e-4) as clear.
*Could not verify*: RayIntersect's exact t range (the wrapper decompile is one call; disassembly needed).
Also ported `Pickup_Update`'s fall-ray start: from the previous tick's translation (obj+0x40 follows
obj+0x30 through the movement pass 0x1336f8:212-231), not the fixed spawn point [M 0x18e148:110-114].
The audit's detail corrections (the ray is lowered by the glist +0x24 centre y, the copy gate is
obj+0xFA & 0x20) are recorded; the port's `models()` reads the glist +0x10 centre for both the take
sphere and the fall rest — a ≤ 0.07 unit rest-height divergence on the armour, noted, not fixed (the
+0x24 centre lives in the same map-object parse as the min/max bounds; nf-formats is out of scope).
Test: `raptor_drops_are_all_taken_when_walked_over` — kills a 07000001 guard through the input path,
walks onto every drop, asserts every drop taken (before the fix the drop logged `los false` forever).

**3. The invisible armour.** The port built placed pickups into the sim only — no drawn instance
anywhere (the only pickup draw hook was the drone-dropped-gun attachment). The game draws the pickup's
own object (`View_DrawObjectGlist` 0x1e6780:43-44 draws obj+0xD8 at obj+0x90); kind 3 is placed-only
(no drop path creates it [M 0x18dda0]), which is why only the armour vanished. Fix (scene.rs): placed
pickups are instanced like doors — Character-layer vertices (`CharVertex.pickup`) posed every frame at
`p.m`, collapsed when taken/hidden; the dropped-gun pose also honours `p.hidden` (the 0x1B twin drop
spawns hidden-but-takeable [M 0x17a2a0:111]). Test: `the_placed_armour_pickup_is_drawn` + gone sister.

**4. The civilian "no" crosshair.** Ported `Check_Target` (0x1a7810, every 6th frame): Bond's 50-unit
view ray; a hit drone with `BLData+0x44 != 1` (the port's `team != 1`) sets the crosshair state to 3
(BLData+0x133) [M :136-139, 181-182], rendered by `HUD_UpdateCrossHair` (0x19e6d0) from `HUDCrossCoords`
state 3 [L 0x2bec48] — the red "no" mark (hud.rs). Aim mode forces cell 1 for non-scope weapons
[0x19e6d0:106-112]. **The decompile has NO trigger block for non-enemy targets** — the fire chain
(0x1a5460 → 0x1a18e0 → 0x12c5a0) never reads +0x133/+0x132/+0x44; the original fires at civilians (they
are excluded from auto-aim lock instead, which the port already did in `auto_aim`). The task asked for a
fire block; the evidence says the block does not exist — ported the crosshair + the existing no-lock-on
and left the trigger alone. *Not modelled*: the weapon-id gate (:152-179 — fists/grenades/dart gun
always show the normal mark) and the +0x2A/+0x2C4 target marking (the port's aimed_at marking covers the
AI arm). Test: `aiming_at_a_non_enemy_shows_the_no_crosshair` (07000001 has no civilian at start — the
test marks a guard non-enemy, the game's own test field, and asserts state 3 vs the enemy/sky arms).

**5. The sniper rifle.** The take gate is `Player_EquipWeapon`'s first-person-model check (0x1a8a58:20,
`hashtable_getitem(+0xDC)`); the port stands it in with the level's skin map. On the slim ISO's
07000001 the sniper's fp skin 0x05000043 is absent (byte-scan [L]; the P2K's 0x05000088 is present),
so the take was refused there — 07000005's archive has both [L]. With the take reachable (07000005),
the fire path had no per-weapon gate left: `the_sniper_fires_after_pickup` takes, equips and fires the
0x24 through the input path. If the user's full-ISO play still refuses the pickup on 07000001, the
NF_PICKUPLOG take line will say so directly.

**Verification**: the five repro tests (shown failing pre-fix); the full suite
`NF_ISO=… cargo test --offline --release -j2 -p nf-game -p nf-formats -p nf-audio -p nf-view --
--test-threads=1` (result recorded below in the commit); an independent audit subagent (8 claims: 7
verified against the decompile, claim 8 partially refuted — the 0x35 fuse finding above — and the fix
updated accordingly).

**Could not verify / left open**: `Collide_RayIntersect`'s endpoint t range (above); the op-1 script
sound's `Rand_Rand(500)` draw (AnimProcessScriptCmds case 1) is not ported — adding it shifts every
seeded RNG stream and needs the established re-picking pass; the crosshair weapon-id gate; the +0x24
fall-rest centre; the guard-grenade fuse (drone.rs, other session's file). No PCSX2 trace replay was
possible in this sandbox.
## 0087 — fix-render: the 0x800 TWEAK/ambient multiply (characters/guns too bright), HUD cut-scene gate

Task: the user's "characters and guns too bright while the world is right" (master 75fbad4), plus the
HUD-visible-in-cut-scenes report; decals if the budget allowed. Branch `s/fix-render`. Sources of
truth: `docs/atlas/gs-leaf.md`, `docs/atlas/render-port-check.md` §1, `docs/atlas/cel.md`.

**Root cause (already documented by atlas-5)** [M 0x1e5888 + 0x1cb178]: the game dims every
`obj+0xF0 & 0x800` object by `tint × obj+0x100..0x102 >> 8` (the VU1 `TAmbient` term), with the
ambient bytes snapped to the object's cel's ambient; the port never applied the multiply.

**What was ported** (files: `crates/nf-view/src/{scene,lib}.rs`; gpu.rs unchanged — the multiply
lives on the vertex bytes, the same carrier the game's VU1 matrix uses):
- `parse_room_cels` (scene.rs): the main map's cel placements with low-16 flags 0xc023/0xc047 become
  `Cel`s — ambient triple 1 = placement params 0/1/2 low bytes (all zero → 0x3c), triple 2 = params
  6/7/8 (0xc047), zone = param 5, bbox = the glist min/max. Pinned by disassembly:
  `parsemap_block_map_data_static` 0x1d1998 builds a 0xb0 stack record whose +0x2c+4k slot is
  placement param k (the params store base is sp+0x2c, the record passed to
  `parseentity_fixup_entity` is sp), and `parseentity_fixup_entity` 0x1d00c0 reads the ambient bytes
  at record+0x2c/0x30/0x34, the zone at +0x40 (0xc047) and the second triple at +0x44/+0x48/+0x4c.
  The bbox is copied raw (record+0x20, 0x20 bytes → cel+0x40) — only the centre at cel+0x80 gets the
  placement transform (`parseentity_transform_bounding_box` 0x1d0fb0) — and the record itself is
  `parsemap_block_entity_params` 0x1d1508's payload+8 mapping (centre/radius/min/max), so the port's
  `MapObject.min/max` are the cel bbox.
- `find_cel` (0x1c8cb0's walk over the flags-0x40000 room cels, inclusive bbox, cap 0x40). [L]
  ee_start_05.bin: 137 runtime cels, exactly 19 with 0x40000; ee_start_07000001.bin: 120/11 — the
  port parses 19 and 11. Multi-cel overlaps: the smallest-volume cel wins (*deviation*; the game
  raycasts up/down — no per-cel object lists to raycast against).
- `Sim::ramp_char_ambient` per tick (the last step of `run`, where
  `control_movement_object_handler` 0x1336f8 calls it in the game): snap once from the 0xff,ff,ff
  sentinel (`control_init_object` 0x134630 / `control_link_object_to_cel` 0x1346b8), then
  `clr_step` = `ClrStep` 0x1e8a48 disassembled — `(target−cur)·0.1`, min ±1 byte. The 0x10000
  doubled targets (night vision) are unreachable in the port (no goggles). View models follow
  Bond's sphere, drone-backed characters their drone, script characters their live entity matrix.
- The multiply: `Scene::posed_vertices` multiplies the Character-layer tail's rgba by
  `(tint × ambient) >> 8 / 255` per character (white tint — `Script_SetColour` is not ported; the
  0x7f/0/0 tint of `Player_InitWeapon` 0x1a7ef8 belongs to the laser-dot object 0x2000132, not the
  view model); static non-cel World instances with glist flags & 0x800 (flagged pickups/props) get
  the same multiply snapped at build; world-cel geometry stays byte-identical (the game's
  `View_DrawCelGlist` 0x1e6538 forces the white tweak). Muzzle flashes/tracers/dropped guns keep 1.0.
- The HUD gate: `nf_view::overlay_for` returns an empty overlay while a script camera runs —
  `Script_CameraStart` 0x1d9140 → `Camera_Enable` 0x1b9920 clears `viewer+0x2a` and `Game_Draw`
  0x1e6f50 skips the whole sprite pass; [D ee_start_07000001.bin] the opening cut-scene has
  viewer[0]/[5] +0x2a = 0 with `ScriptCam`@0x30d100 ≠ 0. All HUD elements hide together in the game;
  the letterbox bars are not ported (G-031).

**Tests** (`crates/nf-view/tests/character_lighting_live.rs`, all NF_ISO, all failed before the fix
— the pre-fix port returned multiplier 1.0 for every character):
- guard + view model = (57,70,86)/255 on 07000005 [L ee_start_05.bin], sister: ≠ 1.0 and ≠ the first
  cel's (27,40,56) [L cel.md] — a naive "level ambient" port fails;
- view model = (40,30,26)/255 [L Bond's cel 0x191c860] and all three drone triples (60,60,60),
  (45,30,30), (80,80,70) [L] hit on 07000001; sisters: no guard at 1.0, room-cel parse = 11;
- world-cel geometry vertex-identical to the source object bytes; sister: 19 room cels [L] and one
  carries (57,70,86);
- the HUD overlay draws before the cut-scene, empties while the script camera is live on 07000001
  (channels armed like the viewer's K key), sister pins the gate to the camera.

**Not done / left open**
- Bullet decals → documented with all functions and offsets in GAPS G-041 (budget).
- The 07000002 bathhouse-civilian skin-texel check → GAPS G-042 (budget; the TWEAK fix covers the
  reported over-bright cause).
- Unverified this pass: `bTweakBrightness`'s reader (still suspected in hand-written VU1); the
  second-triple semantics for 0xc023 cels (the port reuses triple 1 — no observed level sets their
  zone channel); whether dropped-pickup objects carry 0x800 (kept at 1.0).
- Shared-file touches (minimal, noted per the rules): `lib.rs` — `posed_vertices` now delegates to
  `Scene::posed_vertices`, `overlay_for` (new, pub), its two call sites.

**Full suite**: NF_ISO=<iso> cargo test --offline --release -j2 -p nf-game -p nf-formats -p nf-audio
-p nf-view -- --test-threads=1 — see the commit; only the 3 pre-existing `disc_golden` failures
(slim-ISO mismatch) are allowed.

## fix-drone2 — the guard bugs still failing in play (user playtest at 75fbad4)

**Bug 1 — 07000001: no guard ever threw a stun grenade. Conclusion: the port already matches the game; no code change.**
The two param-11 carriers [D 07000001.bin, A3-verified]: guard A skin 0x05000036 at (−30.058, 10.308, 13.443),
param 11 = 0x13 → 3× stun (0x36), switch channel 0x26 (TOUCH plates 311/312); guard B skin 0x0500003A at
(6.950, 6.424, 2.200), param 11 = 0x11 → 1× stun, switch channel 5. What blocks the throw — "the state
they're in", both game-accurate [M]:
- Guard A: DTYPE 2 (param 15) × normal block mode 2 (param 16) → `NDrone2_GetDTYPENEW` 0x14c938 case 2 →
  dtypenew 2 = sniper (alertness +0x50C < 1 at creation; `GetDroneTypeAttackTypeFriend` 0x14cbd8 runs only
  from `DoModeSettingsNEW` 0x14c600 — no runtime re-typing). The sniper states (SniperIdle/Aim/Fire/Reload
  0x15fab0/0x15fc18/0x15fd88/0x15ff80) never call `DroneWeap_CanThrowGrenade` and never enter the combat
  family: its only caller is `DroneFunc_CombatState` 0x148338, cases 0x10 (state 0x68, gated on
  `(+0x568 & 0xFFFF00FF) == 0xA0002`) and 0x18 (state 0x70, ungated — audit). Sniper exits: reload 0x2c,
  aim 0x2a, and melee 0x72 (`NDrone2_CanAltAttack` 0x1549e0, dist ≤ 1.5 — **not ported**, noted as a gap).
- Guard B: dtypenew 0 — a normal combat guard that WOULD throw (`dtype_of` matches GetDTYPENEW), but he
  waits on channel 5 and **nothing on the disc ever raises channel 5**: no trigger outputs it (all 11
  outs listed in the test), the NIS scripts' only event-0xD writes ch 0x0e, no pickup's +0x28 is 5, no
  death channel is 5 [D]. [L work/ee_start_07000001.bin] every drone starts disabled (obj+0xF0 0x8b0).
The headless repro (this session's first test run, shown failing: "no guard reached GRENADE_THROW; last
states [0x2c, 0x1]") + NF_AILOG (can_throw_grenade now logs every evaluation) reproduce exactly this:
guard A cycles SNIPER_FIRE/SNIPER_RELOAD and never evaluates the throw; guard B never leaves WaitSwitch.
`grenade_live.rs` (unchanged) keeps proving the throw machinery itself green. Locked by
`stun_grenade_live.rs::stun_grenade_guards_match_the_game_on_07000001`.

**Bug 2 — 07000002 bathhouse: the frozen "guard next to a civilian". Conclusion: the port matches the atlas; no code change.**
07000002 has no spawners [D], so nothing is "held". 24 of 25 drones wait on switch channels raised by
TOUCH_ONCE plates (ch 0x15: plates 341/383 — 383 is the ground-floor plate beside the civilian; ch 0x17:
plates 342/343/424 — the trio around the ally 0x05000034 at (−45.5, 5.8, 12.2)); the civilian (0x0500004F,
DTYPE 0xC, no channel) is the only skinned character live at start and runs his dtypenew state (0x1c).
After the first ticks every waiter is in WaitSwitch with enabled=false, drawn=false — the fix-core rule —
and wakes into its start state when the plate channel fires (verified for 0x15 by walking Bond over the
real plates and for 0x17 by firing the channel): `bathhouse_live.rs::bathhouse_guards_wake_when_their_plates_fire`
(green). What the user's screenshot shows could not be reproduced in the port's data path: no mechanism
leaves a 07000002 guard drawn-and-frozen (a pre-fix-core build or the deliberate R "reinforcements view"
are the remaining explanations). What I could NOT verify: nf-view's actual render (no GPU in the sandbox).

**Bug 3 — 07000005: the ledge cut-scene left of the castle gate is missing its guards. FIXED (one line).**
The cut-scene is SP 298's NIS 0x06000994 (camera, 1400 ticks), started by TOUCH plate 301 (out 0x43,
lock 0xb3) at (24–26, 31–33, 71–72) — the ledge left of the gate [D]. Streams 1/3 carry the guards
(skins 0x05000030/0x0500002E) and stream 14 Bond (0x05000007). Root cause [M]: the guards' danim
scripts 0x06000996/0x06000997 each hold TWO overlapping opcode-0 commands — a 22-channel face track
(frames 1..1500) and the 222-channel body track (frames 1..1401) [C3, C4-verified]. The game starts
every op-0 command whose window the script time enters (`AnimProcessScriptCmds` 0x1c1b38 → `AnimSeqSet`,
in command order) and the palette lets the later-started track own the shared bones. The port's
`script_frame` (nf-game/src/anim.rs) picked the FIRST covering command — the 22-channel face track —
which cannot pose the 73-bone skeleton (`fits` false), so the view's pose chain returned None and both
guards drew nothing while Bond (single-sequence script 0x06000995) showed fine. Fix: `script_frame` now
returns the LAST covering op-0 command (shared-file change, minimal). Fail-before:
`ledge_live.rs::the_guard_anim_scripts_resolve_to_sequences_that_fit_their_skeletons` (failed pre-fix:
"sequence 040007fa must fit skin 05000030's skeleton"), green after; sister inside the same test pins
the single-sequence drone start scripts (060002f2) to their only sequence. Also:
`the_ledge_cutscene_creates_its_guard_characters` (the sim creates and animates all three cut-scene
characters — that part already worked).

## fix-level — level transitions and level-end exits (07000005 → 07000006, 07000001 → 07000002)

**Bug 1 — the window disappeared during the level transition while audio kept playing (07000005 castle
door / truck end → reload). FIXED.**
- Root cause [M port code]: `nf-view`'s `RedrawRequested` reload path called `load()` for the next
  archive and then set `self.gfx = None` ("force a Gfx re-init"). winit's `ApplicationHandler::resumed`
  — the only place `Gfx` was ever created — runs at event-loop start-up, not when `gfx` becomes `None`,
  so after the reload the `Arc<Window>` was dropped (the window closed) and the app sat on a headless
  event loop: the sim kept ticking and `self.sound` (the NEW level's bank — `Output` owns the cpal
  stream, so the old level's audio stopped on the reload) kept playing. Exactly the user's report.
- Fix (crates/nf-view/src/lib.rs): the renderer is rebuilt **in place** (`gpu::Renderer::new` with the
  new scene on the existing device/queue/surface/window); `Gfx` is never dropped. The reload error path
  already kept `Gfx`. Not headless-verifiable (no GPU/window in the sandbox) — verified by code reading
  and left for the user's playtest.
- Fidelity fix in the same path [M LoaderLoad 0x1d4a00]: the archive name is now
  `level_archive_name(code) = format!("{:08x}.bin", code & 0xff0f_ffff)` — the game masks the loader
  nibble OFF before `sprintf("%8.8x.bin")`; `ResetMap_LevelToLoad` (0x1d3800, param_3 == 0) remaps
  0x07000006 → 0x07100006 into GameState+8 and the load masks it back. For today's levels both forms
  agree (the trigger's out value carries the raw code [L trigger.md ext+0x20 = 0x07000006]); the mask
  pins the game's behaviour for any code that carries the 0x00100000 bit.
- Tests (crates/nf-view/tests/level_reload_live.rs, new file): `level_archive_name_masks_the_loader_nibble`
  (fails against the pre-fix inline `format!("{next:08x}.bin")` for the remapped 0x07100006) and
  `reload_after_load_level_exit_loads_07000006` (drives the route-a chain to `level_exit`, then runs the
  viewer's reload step: `07000006.bin` parses, builds a sim, `sim.level == 0x07000006`; sister: the
  unmasked `07100006.bin` is not a FILES.BIN name and must fail).

**Bug 2 — the 07000005 truck ride does not end the level. DIAGNOSED, NOT FIXED (evidence recorded).**
Reproduced headless with the real input path (`truck_ride_to_the_castle_ends_the_level`, `#[ignore]`d
with the diagnosis): Bond at the gatehouse plate → the cut-scene hands him onto the truck (t≈2100) →
the ride works (bond carried 92,20,104 → 29.9,38.4,52.0, parked with Bond in the back) → ch 0x71 (the
truck-bed touch, parented to the truck) is on for the whole ride → ch 0x22 fires on the way through the
gatehouse (t≈3700) → the gate guard spawns and stands at his post, ch 0x72 on (t≈3700). The chain stops
at **ch 0x70** (the parked-position TouchOnce, player mask 0x8, script 0x06000A22 stream 6, entity
0x0200047F — NOT parented to the truck [D]): its plate is a flat quad at y = 37.7418 spanning
(28.80..30.87, 48.38..52.18), and the port's riding Bond parks with feet at y = 38.376 — the 0.55-radius
touch capsule ([M Player_Collision 0x194DF0: 0x3f0ccccd = 0.55]; axis points feet−0.4+0.55 and up) misses
the plate by ≈0.24 m. In the game the plate lies at bed-floor height (parked truck root 36.05 + the bed
hull bottom ≈1.69 ≈ 37.74 [D]), so the game's Bond stands on it and the touch fires. Fixing this needs
either the game's collide-stage contact geometry for triggers (the writer of `obj+0xD0`, untraced) or
the port's bed stand height (`drone.rs` — a shared file this task must not retune without game
evidence). Everything else in the chain (mux 316, SP #320, EndLevel event 0x11 → ch 0x1D, LOAD_LEVEL
118 → 0x07000006) is verified working by the existing level_end_live tests.

**Bug 3 — the 07000001 level-end door does nothing on E. FOUND + mechanism verified; the gap is the
un-ported mission layer, not the exit code.**
- The disc's ONLY exit on 07000001 [D placements]: **Touch #180** (0xEB, out 0x10, mask 0x18, filters
  [0xE = the player, 0x0500004F = a drone skin], lock 0x63) at (−33.1, 2.9, 14.5) — 44 collision tris,
  the port builds it with its volume — and **LOAD_LEVEL #18** (0xE8, next 0x07000002, gate 0x10, key 0)
  at (−33.2, 1.7, 17.1) whose target object is "Load Point" (flags 0x30, **no collision** — so neither
  the game's E-path (`Player_Activate` 0x1a5170 finds objects only via `Collide_SphereIntersect` on
  collision, decomp read this session) nor the port's can ever E-activate it; it is not an E door).
  The chain: Bond AND a skin-0x0500004F NPC in the plate volume → ch 0x10 pulses → LL #18 fires →
  07000002 (the campaign's next level [D mission-data.md]).
- The NPC (drone placement 161, skin 0x0500004F) starts **disabled waiting on ch 0xB** [L
  ee_start_07000001: +0x134 = 0xB, +0x136 = 0, state +0x10C = 1 = Disabled, start state 0x1C]. No
  writer for ch 0xB exists on the disc (placements of every trigger family + every type-5 and type-7
  script scanned) — the enable comes from the game's mission layer, which the port does not have.
- `level_end_07000001_needs_bond_and_the_0x4f_npc_on_the_plate`: Bond alone on the plate → no ch 0x10,
  no exit (sister); with ch 0xB set (the game's enable state) and both actors on the plate →
  `level_exit = Some(0x07000002)` at the next tick. The port's Touch AND-chain, lock, calc clear and
  LOAD_LEVEL gate all behave exactly as the atlas says.

already corrected this; the 0x07000066 in U-048's first sentence is the stale value (there is no

## 0088 — fix-render2: the merged lighting's follow-ups (cut-scene chars, pickups, truck, merge regression), the safe World cull

Task: the user's check of fix-render's lighting (merged) plus the playtest 2026-10-11 rendering
follow-ups. Branch `s/fix-render2` from master d589c76. Files: `crates/nf-view/src/{scene,gpu}.rs`
(scene.rs is the only shared-file touch; lib.rs/hud.rs untouched).

**The merge regression (found first).** The merge d589c76 ("combine add_instance: their 0x800 mult +
my pickup slot") dropped fix-player2's pickup branch in `add_instance` — `pickup: Some(pk)` was
never pushed as a CharVertex, so placed-pickup vertices entered the Character tail without one, the
vertex↔CharVertex zip in `posed_vertices` misaligned, and every draw group after the first pickup
posed wrongly while the pickups never posed. Restored (fix-player2 eb1564b scene.rs:1039 is the
line the merge lost). Test: `placed_pickup_charvertices_survived_the_merge` (failed pre-fix:
0 pickup CharVertices, counts unequal).

**Cut-scene characters over-bright (user check 1).** Root cause: `Sim::characters_script_pos`
resolved script characters through `script_entity`, which matches only `Obj::Entity` — script Anim
characters (Obj::Anim) never got an ambient target and kept the 0xff sentinel → multiplier 1.0.
Fixed: the position is now the live Anim's root-bone world translation (`script_anim` →
`script_frame` → `local_pose`/`world_pose`; the Anim object sits at the origin and the sequence's
root carries it — nis.rs, `AnimSeqTick` 0x1c28d0). [L ee_start_07000001.bin] the opening cut-scene's
script-created character objects (0x018f5790 flags 0x890, 0x018f6a30/0x018f6b90 flags 0x860) all
read ambient (40,30,26) — cel 0x191c860, the courtyard. Test:
`cutscene_script_characters_dim_to_their_cel_ambient` (failed pre-fix: sentinel 1.0).

**The truck (user check 3).** The truck is the script Anim object of skin 0x05000005 (nine rigid
parts [D script-player.md]); its nine game objects carry obj+0xF0 = 0x8880 with ambient (57,70,86)
[L ee_start_05.bin 0x0137C8A0…]. The same Anim-position fix dims it. Test:
`the_truck_takes_the_0x800_ambient` (failed pre-fix).

**Dropped weapons and placed pickups (user check 2).** `Pickup_Create` (0x18dda0) FORCES
`obj+0xF0 = glist_flags & ~0x2000 | 0x840` — every pickup is character-lit — EXCEPT kind 3 (armour:
0x800 cleared, 0x80000 set) and kind 6 (007 bonus: 0x800 cleared) [M decompile :137-151]. The port's
placed-pickup and dropped-gun vertices now dim by the cel ambient at the pickup's live matrix, gated
by that kind rule (NOT the mesh's glist flags — the slim ISO's one placed pickup, model 0200092a, is
kind 6 and correctly stays untinted). Tests: `placed_pickups_follow_the_pickup_create_gate` (pins
the kind-6 exemption), `dropped_guns_dim_to_the_cel_ambient` (kills a 07000001 guard through the
input path and asserts the drop's drawn multiplier equals the ambient bytes; failed pre-fix at 1.0).

**The first guard too dark (user check 4).** Not reproduced at the evidence points: [L
ee_start_07000001.bin] all 15 drones' (position → ambient) pairs are reproduced by the port's snap
under the smallest-volume cel tie-break (`the_first_guard_snaps_to_the_game_ambient`, drone 0 at
(−4.92, 6.34, −0.09) → (20,20,20) cel 0x191f0e0 INCLUDED — the game's own value). `build_FindCel`
(0x1c8cb0 disassembly) raycasts each matched cel's own object list (up 256 max, down limited by the
up hit, nearest wins, else first match); the port has no per-cel object lists — a shared-geometry
raycast with bbox attribution was tried and mis-attributed vertically-adjacent geometry (drone 1 in
the two-cel courtyard overlap read (20,20,20) where the game reads (40,30,26)), so the
smallest-volume tie-break stays, with the disassembly documented in `Sim::cel_at`. Left open: the
user's symptom may live in a guard walking through an overlap the snapshot does not cover — needs a
PCSX2 trace of that guard's walk.

**R3 doors.** The evidence REFUTES the tint hypothesis: the 07000005 door models' glist flags are 0x0
[D] and `Door_Create` (0x136100) only calls `Control_SetGList` — the game never dims doors through
the 0x800 path. The port's doors stay 1.0, which matches the game. Pinned negatively by
`doors_carry_no_0x800_and_stay_untinted` (any future tint fix must re-measure first). (Also: the
pre-fix code tinted doors/searchlight parts with character 0's multiplier through the
`mults.get(cv.character)` fall-through — restored the explicit 1.0 branches.)

**Performance (user check 5 / R4).** The renderer submitted every material every frame (the cull was
off by default after A-11's vanish bug: "the truck and the HUD vanished by view direction"). fix: the
default cull now scopes to the static World layer only — its spheres are exact (placement-matrix
transform of the glist sphere, built once); everything posed per frame (Character/Effect: doors,
pickups, the truck, searchlight parts, flashes, tracers) and the sky are exempt, and the HUD draws
from its own buffer. NF_CULL still enables the full test cull. Measured from the level-start cameras
(headless, `party_levels_cull_the_static_bulk_from_the_start_view`): 07000006 — 1040 of 4438 World
draws submitted (77 % skipped; 4651 materials total); 07000007 — 4526 of 4869 still inside the

next lever is the portal cull (G-016), not a sphere-tuning fix. GPU time itself is not measurable in
this sandbox (no GPU); the draw-count relief is the CPU/headless proxy the task asked for
(NF_DRAWS=1 prints the live counters).

## 0089 — fix-ladder: the ladder system (Ladder_Create/Player_CollLadder/Player_Climb) and the swim substate (Player_InWater + case 3 + Player_MonitorAir)

Task: the user's 07000002 report — Bond starts in an underground bunker and can't get out (the exit is a
ladder; ladders weren't implemented), and the level's water is walk-on-top instead of swimmable. Branch
`s/fix-ladder` from master 4b199d0. Files: new `crates/nf-game/src/ladder.rs`,
`crates/nf-game/src/player.rs` (the substate functions only), `crates/nf-view/src/scene.rs` (placement
wiring + the tick context), new `crates/nf-view/tests/fix_ladder_live.rs`, docs (`atlas/ladder.md`,
`atlas/wire-grapple.md` correction, `systems/levels.md`), `lib.rs` (one `pub mod ladder;` line).

**Research (before any code).** The substate machinery was already documented (wire-grapple.md: substate 1
= Player_Climb 0x196310, hit class 0x2D → CollLadder) but unported — grep found no ladder/climb code in
crates/. Ported whole from the decompile:
- `Ladder_Create` 0x1966c0 [M disasm]: placement type 0x22 → control_create_object(4) (instance 4 bytes:
  inst+0=0, inst+2=placement param 1, unread), class 0x2D; rotation passed through UNMODIFIED — the
  wire-grapple atlas's "rot.z is negated … as for ladders" note was wrong (corrected there).
- `Player_CollLadder` 0x196118 [M]: walk into the ladder attaches (not use-key driven): |AngleDiff
  (player, ladder) | > π/2 (Vec_AngleDifference 0x1e2b78 = wrap(b−a)), y window bottom=cy−r+1.0 /
  top=cy+r+0.85 (raised to bottom+0.02 first), snap to centre+fwd(yaw)·0.5, ChangeSubState(1),
  WeaponNone, regrab/mode/+0x130/+0x884.
- `Player_Climb` 0x196310 [M]: yaw clamp+ease toward ladder.yaw+π (ease uses the pre-clamp diff),
  Player_Move(0) (no walk), BLData+0x50 zeroed, the climb 0.02·fwd units/tick (FRAME_RATE_MUL=1
  [L 0x30d0d8]) = 1.2 u/s; top dismount +0.6 local-forward push, action (7) dismount −0.05, bottom
  dismount; every dismount regrab=60, +0x942=substate, +0x14=0. The BLData+0x10..0x1F wish vector is
  ZEROED EVERY TICK by Player_Update (obj+0xF4==1 branch [M disasm 0x193830-0x19383c: Vec_Zero(s2+16),
  Vec_Zero(s2+48)]) — so the +0x14 climb delta and the ±0x18 pushes are one-tick displacements (the
  port consumes them as `vel`/`push_fwd` the same way).
- Swim [M]: cel+0x90 = the water surface (build_alloc_cel 0x1c93f8 defaults −500.0;
  parseentity_fixup_entity 0x1d00c0 sets it to the entity bbox max y — cel+0x54 — for flag word 0xC023,
  −500.0 for 0xC047; the bbox is the glist copy at 0x1d1998 amemcpy(cel+0x40, glist+0x20, 0x20)).
  Player_InWater 0x195e50 is Player_SSWalk's FIRST statement (y−0.3 < surface → ChangeSubState(3) — case
  3 in the Player_Update dispatch is the swim, not only riding); case 3 = Player_Move(1.0) + the
  surface−0.3 up-velocity clamp + the grounded exit; Player_Collision 0x194df0 applies NO gravity below
  the surface. Player_MonitorAir 0x191a70: air −5/s under (from 100), +20/s over ANY cel, drown
  Player_HandlePain(0x40000000 = 2.0, type 7) every 30 ticks below 1.0 (the 2.0 was caught by the audit;
  0x40000000 is 2.0f, not 0.5f).

**Disc data** [D]: 4 ladders on 07000002 (the bunker exit ≈(−26.9, 2.3, 42.2), world top 5.96), water
surfaces 3.76–4.34 on 5 cels; 9 more levels carry ladders and 07000016 one water cel — the full table is
in docs/systems/levels.md (new §"Ladders and water, per level", from the sweep test).

**Reproduce-first.** `prefix_bond_cannot_leave_the_bunker` (run on stashed master, not committed):
Bond placed at the bunker ladder's face, 900 forward ticks → y 1.051 → 1.097: "SYMTOM REPRODUCED ON
MASTER". The committed tests assert the fixed behaviour through `nf_view::load` + `Sim::step_bond` (the
viewer's own play path):
- `ladder_walk_into_it_climbs_to_the_garden_and_walks_away`: walk into the ladder → substate 1 → reaches
  the garden (y > 5.2), dismounts to walk, walks away, net climb > 2. Sister: the climb's height gain.
- `walk_into_water_enters_the_swim_substate`: a grid search finds deep water inside a 0xC023 cel box
  (the moat cel's box starts at −0.73), Bond placed there → substate 3, y−0.3 < surface. Sister: dry
  bunker start never swims.
- `ladder_and_water_counts_per_level`: the per-level sweep (docs table); sister: 07000002 ≥ 4 ladders.

**Audit (independent subagent, claims + decompile).** All 15 decompile claims CONFIRMED (2 with
corrections), and it caught 4 port bugs, all fixed: (1) double vertical integration in swim (physics
integrated the stale vel[1], then swim_tick integrated again) — the swim y integration now happens once,
after the clamp; (2) air never refilled on land (the game's refill branch runs for the −500 default cel
too); (3) drown damage 0.5 → 2.0 (0x40000000); (4) the ladder grab was unreachable from the swim
substate (the game excludes only substates 1/2) — swim_tick now runs the grab scan. Also adopted: the
dismount writes +0x14=0 and does NOT clear +0x94D.

**Deviations, tagged [S] in docs/atlas/ladder.md**: the grab hit-shape is the ladder's axis column (the
game's per-object HITTEST shape isn't recoverable this pass); the climb-yaw ease always runs (AnimObj
flag bit 0 unresolved); the climb "hit below" flag 8 is the port's floor ray (the game uses the
CollisionHandler's hit list); vertical swim controls are jump/crouch (the game's dive input unresolved);
the head bone is the eye; climb anims / the underwater fade visual / the air HUD / breath sounds are not
ported (fields exposed: `water_fade`, `underwater`).

**Verified**: `cargo test --release -p nf-game --lib` 65/65; the full suite
`NF_ISO=<iso> cargo test --offline --release -j2 -p nf-game -p nf-formats -p nf-audio -p nf-view --
--test-threads=1` (see the commit message for the counts; only the 3 allowed slim-ISO disc_golden
failures). Determinism: no RNG draws added (the ladder/water paths consume none in the game [M grep of
the six touched decomp files]); fixed 60 Hz; no wall-clock or HashMap order in Sim.

## fix-player3 — the player follow-ups (user playtest at afc60ed): reload-from-empty, mid-reload switch, the thrown grenade, the armour glow, drop/crosshair pins

Branch `s/fix-player3` from master 4b199d0 (which already carried the merged fix-render2). Every fix has
a headless NF_ISO test in `crates/nf-view/tests/fix_player3_live.rs` driving the real input path
(`nf_view::load` + `Sim::step_bond`), shown failing on the pre-fix build (git stash of the four source
files) and green after.

**3. Reload from empty plays wrong — FIXED (gun.rs + scene.rs).** The reload key and auto-reload
branches of `Player_WeaponFiring` (0x1a5460:395-498) share one script tail: the +0xA4 loop queues at
**1.35×** (`AnimScriptAddSpeed`, disasm 0x1a62d0 — the decompiler dropped the hash), **starting at
frame 6** for flag-0x1000 weapons (AnimListBuild +0x90 = 6.0, disasm 0x1a6300-31c), with tick count
ceil((len−6)/1.35). The port played +0xA4 at 1.0 from frame 0 and never used its own computed
`reload_ticks`. Retail scan [L ee_start_05.bin]: the P2K (flags68 0x1004) and Raptor (0x100C) both
reload this way; only SPAS-12 0x1c/0x1d has +0xA8 (state 5) or +0xAC. Also ported: a non-shell weapon
(flags68 & 0x100 == 0) goes STRAIGHT from state 6 to idle — LAB_001a3678 (0x1a3678-0x1a369c) plays
+0xA0, sets state 0, `Input_ClearAction(9)`; the port's spurious state-7 hop (with +0xAC = 0 → one
tick of view_script 0) is gone (shell weapons keep the +0xAC path). Branch B (auto-reload) zeroes the
refire timer [M 0x1a6244] and its trigger condition is the fire EDGE ("not newly pressed", disasm
0x1a61d0), not "released" — so holding the trigger still auto-reloads, as in the game (the take and
the auto-reload land on the same tick in the repro). Test:
`reload_from_empty_plays_the_1_35x_loop_and_lands_on_idle` (pre-fix: speed 1.0).

**4. Switching mid-reload breaks shooting — FIXED (scene.rs).** `Player_WeaponChange`
(0x1a6f80:33-47) refuses every switch while the view state is in {1,3,5,6,7,8,9,0xb,0xd..0x10} — the
reload states 5/6/7 are in the refused set: a request during a reload is DROPPED (nothing written) and
the holster can only start once the reload completed. The port set `switch_request` whenever
`switch_state == 0 && !fire_busy` — no reload check — and the holster started mid-reload, stomping the
view script and wedging the fire path. Fix: the step_bond gate and run()'s holster start both require
`reload_state == 0` (a pending request now waits, as the game's ungated +0x63 writers do). Test:
`switching_mid_reload_is_refused_and_firing_recovers` (pre-fix: the request was set mid-reload; the
"start reload → switch → switch back → fire" flow now fires).

**5. The thrown grenade — FIXED (grenade.rs + one line in drone.rs, both shared files — minimal).**
Three root causes [M]:
- the flight: `Bullet_update`'s movement tail (0x12f040-0x12f058) moves `pos += fVar16 · velocity`
  with fVar16 = speed · FRAME_RATE_MUL (= 1 at the fixed 60 Hz) and velocity the per-tick displacement
  (unit direction · speed, re-normalised after the gravity add, `Vec_NormaliseLen` storing the length
  into BU+0xF8). The port moved `pos += velocity · REC_FRAME_RATE` — 60× too slow: the grenade
  crawled at ~0.17 u/s (repro: max horizontal distance 0.58 units) and the fuse expired at Bond's feet
  ("the throw doesn't really happen, no explosion").
- the fuse: `Bullet_init` (0x12c5a0:103,196-223) hardcodes BU+0xFC = 210 (300 with +0x70 & 0x10000,
  420 for the mine 0x37); `weapon_data+0x1C` (5000) is the max-travelled range — a SILENT state-4
  death [M Bullet_update case 1], not the fuse. The guard throw passed `f32_at(0x1c).max(210.0)` = 5000
  (the fix-player2 audit's noted deviation) — guard grenades never fuse-exploded.
- the blast damage: `Explode_Create`'s damage arg is the hardcoded 100, not weapon_data+0x0C (the
  damage MULTIPLIER, 0.0 for the frag 0x35) [M disasm 0x12cd98/0x12ce18: `addiu $t2,$zero,0x64` →
  EXPLODEINFO+0x28 → `Explode_Propagate`'s amount via `Explode_CollisionHandler` 0x17cde0:13-15;
  radius = $f12 = weapon_data+0x08 = 10.0 [L]]. With damage 0.0 the port's explosion damaged nobody.
Also the first tick now steps (0.5 + FRand(0.5)) · speed [M 0x12e7c0] (the draw was already there, the
step was discarded). Tests: `thrown_grenade_flies_and_explodes_with_sound_and_damage` (pre-fix: 0.58
units, no explosion observed) + fix_player2's grenade test updated to track the grenade through its
life (it now flies AND explodes inside that test's 80-tick window — game-accurate).

**2. Armour glow — ported (scene.rs).** Kind-3 armour carries the 0x80000 flag [M `Pickup_Create`
0x18dda0:145-146]; `View_SetupRenderModes_Tweak` (0x1e5888:22-44) multiplies its tint by `FlashMod`
while the viewer's camera (viewer+0xC0) is within 4.0 units of the pickup's world-sphere centre
(squared distance < 16.0) and option byte DAT_002a38d4 is set (1 at level start [L both snapshots]).
`FlashMod` (Check_Target 0x1a7810:95-97) is a 1 Hz sine shimmer in [0.5, 1.0] off GameState+0x76
(psiGetTimeIn100ths); the port feeds it its tick count (phase = frame/60 s) — render-side only. No
corona, no additive pass: the pulse rides the same vertex-colour multiply as the ambient dim (the
port's camera is Bond's eye, first person as in play). `nf_view::scene::flash_mod(frame)` is pub.
Test: `armour_glow_pulses_when_bond_is_close` (frame 45 → FlashMod exactly 0.75; near = tint × 0.75,
far = 1.0; pre-fix: near == far == 1.0).

**1. Guard death drops — NO REPRO, the port already matches the game (pin test added).**
`DroneWeap_DropWeapon` (0x17a2a0) creates exactly ONE visible pickup — the base weapon, kind 0
(disasm 0x17a404-08: `$a3 = 0`); the only second pickup is the 0x1A twin (kind 1, id 0x1B,
clip·(FRand(0.5)+0.25), disasm 0x17a428-84) which the game hides immediately (`obj+0xF0 |= 0x10`).
All Pickup_CreateSimple/Create callers scanned: no death path creates a VISIBLE kind-1 pickup
(0x14b158 kind 0; 0x17a2a0 kinds 0 + 1-hidden; 0x190810 MP-only, same pattern; `Pickup_CreateFromSet`
0x18f1b0's visible small twin is the MP spawn-set, not a death drop). Hidden = not drawn [M
`View_AddObjects` 0x1e62d8:33 `(flags & 0x8010) == 0`; `View_AddForcedObjects` 0x1e5fb8:85-89] and

**6. The civilian no-shoot "block" — the code has none (pin test + addresses).** BLData+0x133
(crosshair state) is written by `Check_Target` (0x1a7810:101-204: +0x132 clear/mark, +0x133 = 2/3) and
read ONLY by `HUD_UpdateCrossHair` (0x19e6d0:69 — display) and cleared in `Player_InitWeapon`

## fix-render3 — what fix-render2 didn't reach (jitter regression, 07000007 view lag, cel cull, G-041)

The task's lighting bullets (cut-scene characters, dropped guns / placed pickups, the truck) were
already fixed by fix-render2 (WORKLOG 0088, on master; tests in render2_live.rs re-run green in this
suite) — the first-guard item stays as fix-render2 left it (not reproduced at any [L] position; needs
a PCSX2 trace of the walking guard).

**The 07000006 frame jitter — measured, mechanism identified.** Headless timings on 07000006 through
the real path: `step_bond` **4.1 ms/tick**, `animate` **5.8 ms/frame**, `posed_vertices` **14.4
ms/frame** (76 characters, 379 k character vertices), `ramp_char_ambient` 0.0036 ms/tick (negligible).
The viewer runs 1–8 sim ticks per render frame (fixed 60 Hz logic decoupled from the display rate), so
the sim alone bursts 4–33 ms per frame — a variable per-frame cost that presents as jitter. The sim
tick cost is the dominant term and predates fix-render2's merge (fix-drone3's party-civilian AI runs
in the same ticks; the render-side additions were measured at ≈1 ms). fix-render3's render-side cut:
the fix-render2 ambient multipliers for pickups / dropped guns / script entities were computed inside
the per-vertex closure (per-vertex `find_cel` scans + pickup scans); they now run once per distinct
key per frame (a `Sim::ambient_lookups` counter pins it: **2 lookups per posed_vertices pass** on
07000005 where the truck's nine 0x8880 parts previously triggered thousands). posed_vertices: 14.4 →
**13.2 ms/frame**. What remains on 07000006 is the per-tick AI cost and the irreducible 379 k-vertex
pose+copy — a main-agent-level item (pose caching between ticks, or the AI tick budget).

**The 07000007 view-direction lag — measured, the honest finding.** From the start camera: looking
forward submits 4526 World draws (fix-render2's number — all 32 room cels' bboxes genuinely intersect
that frustum), looking away 64 (the sphere cull drops 97 %+), left 1379, right 148, down 593. The
direction dependence is the frustum itself; the start view's cost is front-facing geometry, so the
lever is OCCLUSION, not frustum refinement.

**The cel visibility cull (G-016, the decompile-visible half).** Every static World draw now carries
its room cel (`Material.cel` = `build_FindCel` 0x1c8cb0 over the placement's world centre — the same
lookup `build_LinkToRoom` 0x1c9680 uses to link the game's objects), and the renderer frustum-tests
each room cel's bbox per frame as an 8-corner box test (`box_outside` — the port's reading of
`View_AddCels` 0x1e6ba0's `Vision_InView` frustum/bbox test) and skips attributed draws in invisible
cels. `NF_NOCELCULL` disables; NF_DRAWS counts the cel-culled draws separately. Measured: attribution
4438/4438 on 07000006, 3820/3820 on 07000002, 4861/4869 on 07000007; the test relieves nothing on
today's three problem views (pinned in render3_live.rs) — the portal-graph traversal that would cut
the start view needs map block 0x21 (the pCelList record adjacency), which `nf-formats` does not
expose and this task's file set does not include, and the game's own traversal evidence is open
(cel.md's caveat). G-016 stays open with the measured numbers.

**Not reached (out of budget, unchanged from GAPS):** G-041 bullet decals (the measurement is complete
in GAPS; the port shape is specified — a new effects module + a 200-entry FIFO in the Sim), R2 (the
decal/shadow depth rule), O5 (searchlight beam/corona), G-042 (the bathhouse skin-texel histogram —
needs the skin's texture identified on the disc).

**Tests**: `crates/nf-view/tests/render3_live.rs` — 3 NF_ISO tests (the 07 direction-dependence pin,
the 06/02 attribution + eye-cel vanish guard, the per-key lookup budget), shown failing against the
pre-attribution code (first run: attribution 0, no relief) and green after.
## fix-level2 — carry-over between levels and per-level rules (playtest 2026-10-11 F1/F2/F4/F5)

Research (general-purpose subagents, then re-verified in the decomp by me):
- The spawn point: `parsemap_create_dynamic_objects` (0x1d04f0) case 0x24 appends a `player_start`
  entry per placement (0xE0 bytes; pos, rot, kind 1, the 0xB0 param block) [M 0x195c00]; param 0 lands
  at entry+0x50 = the GATE switch channel. `Player_Start` (0x190fd0) is a two-pass scan: first kind-1
  entry whose gate is 0 or whose channel is on, else the first kind-1 entry [M]. The gate is written by
  the previous level's exit: `Trigger_Activate` (0x1b2318:91-107) writes the success channel (ext+0x2C)
  when the auto channel (ext+0x28) is on, else the fallback (ext+0x2A) — BOTH before the load.
  `Init_SwitchChannels` runs only when `IsWarmReset == 0` [M 0x1d5080], so the channel globals survive
  the warm transition into the start scan. [D] 07000005's exit #118 (gate 0x1D, success 0x1D, fallback
  0x1F) → 07000006's starts: 496 gate 0x1D (the truck-ride spawn), 510 gate 0x1F, 511 gate 0x1E — the
  castle-door route (gate off → fallback 0x1F) must spawn at 510, the truck route (ch 0x1D already on →
  success 0x1D) at 496. That is playtest F1's "entry matching the route".
- The carry-over: `Player_RamSave` (0x195670) → global RamSave 0x2b9440: BL+0x170 (0x42 spare ammo),
  BL+0x1B4 (0x558 weapon entries), BL+0x70C (0x33 key ring), SSys/PlrMissionStats/BondMoments,
  switch_channels{_time,_hold,_prev}, health BL+0x894, armour BL+0x8B0, weapon M_CONTROL+0x63 [M].
  `Player_RamLoad` (0x1957a8) is entirely gated on `IsWarmReset` and restores them; it runs inside
  `Player_InitWeapon`'s (0x1a7ef8) per-level switch on GameState+0x0C: case 0x7000006 = RamLoad +
  request = BL+0x934, falling back to the fresh-0x7000005 loadout when `Upgrade_Weapon(6)` (the P2K,
  2 [L UpgradedHandguns 0x2bee08 = [2,4,6,8], Upgrades 0]) is unowned; case 0x7000007 = RamLoad +
  InitAmmoWeapons + armour 0 + equips (P2K 0x30 rds, 0x4a 999, 0x50 0, 0x54 0) + request 1 (FISTS);
  case 0x7000008 = RamLoad + request = saved, fallback into case 7 [M].
- The party weapon lock: `Player_Weapon` (0x1a24c8:242-275): on 0x7000007 with ch 0x48 OFF the cycle
  routes to `Player_WeaponChange(±1, mode 2)` (fists-only + click 0x1DB); ch 0x48 on with
  `switch_channels_prev[0x48]` off → the request becomes `Upgrade_Weapon(6)` [M]. ch 0x48 is written by
  TouchOnce placements 411/412 on 07000007 [D]. The party is 07000007 (the dressing script at the end of
  07000006 loads 07000007 [D nf-extract nis]) — the playtest's "party level 07000006" is off by one.
- The death cut-scene: the plunge/death NIS is LEVEL DATA — plunge TouchOnce triggers (out 0xBE on
  07000005, 0x7C on 07000008; mask 8) → ScriptPlayer (0x06000952 / 0x06000991, mask bit 1) [D]. There is
  NO death NIS in the player death path (Player_CheckForDeath 0x190810 sets ch 0x5E + Music_Event(6,1)
  only [M]). The E-path must never fire them: `Trigger_Activate` begins its type-1/2/0xD arms with
  `if ((mask & 4) == 0) return;` [M 0x1b2318:23-57]. The port's `activate_request` lacked the gate.

Fixes (commit "fix-level2: carry-over, per-exit spawn, party weapon lock, plunge use-key gate"):
- triggers.rs: the mask&4 gate in `activate_request`'s TOUCH_ONCE/TOUCH arms + the `gone` (type-99)
  guard on the LOAD_LEVEL E-path (audit finding).
- player.rs (new, carry-over/spawn section): `RamSave` (capture/restore — the port-modelled subset of
  0x195670), `LevelStart` + `pick_start` (0x190fd0), `init_ammo_weapons` (0x1a17f8), `init_level_loadout`
  (0x1a7ef8 cases 0x7000005/6/7/8 + default → `Inventory::level_start`, common tail), the weapon lock
  (`weapon_lock_input` / `weapon_lock_auto_draw`, 0x1a24c8:242-275).
- nf-view lib.rs: `load_with_carry` — the reload captures RamSave at the exit, parses the type-0x24
  starts (gate = param 0, yaw = rotation[1], the "Player1" convention), runs the two-pass pick with the
  carried channels, re-stands Bond, runs the per-level loadout and sets the switch request; the lock
  gates the input each tick and the ch-0x48 rising edge auto-draws the P2K (App.prev_lock_ch).

Tests (crates/nf-view/tests/level_carry_live.rs, 8, all NF_ISO, all driving load_with_carry/step_bond):
plunge_trigger_ignores_the_use_key (F5), castle_door_route_spawns_at_the_matched_entry (F1, the user's
symptom) + truck_route_spawns_at_the_truck_entry (sister), warm_transition_carries_health_armour_weapons_
ammo (F2) + cold_load_starts_fresh (sister), cold_07000005_loadout_matches_the_snapshot (the [L] anchor),
party_level_starts_unarmed_and_locked (F4), use_key_still_activates_gated_triggers_and_load_level
(regression). Pre-fix demonstration: with the four fixes toggled out (mask&4 → false, pick_start → first
entry, init_level_loadout → default case, lock disabled) exactly the four bug tests FAIL and their
sisters still pass; toggles restored (git diff clean against the commit).

Independent audit (general-purpose subagent): 5/5 C-side claims VERIFIED with exact lines; findings
folded in: the LOAD_LEVEL `gone` guard (fixed); the rest recorded below.

Could not verify / left open (evidence recorded, no guessing):
- The walk-in graze: Bond's touch capsule (Toucher::player, the trigger-port-check stand-in) can contact
  the plunge volumes whose meshes top out at cliff-path height — e.g. near the 07000005 wire the port's
  walking capsule reaches the volume (reproduced headless once via the walk-in path during development).
  The game does not fire there; the real gate is the collide-stage contact semantics (which shape of the
  player the trigger contacts use), untraced. The E-path — the user's reported symptom — is fixed and
  tested; the walk-in needs the Trigger_Hit contact pipeline (trigger-port-check owner).
- The SP state-0 gate (SP_Update 0x1dbda8:84-98: Bond health > 0 && Mission_Status ∈ {0,1}) is not
  ported — nis.rs has no health/mission access on its update path without touching files this task does
  not own.
- `DAT_002a373c` (InitAmmoWeapons' boot flag) is the all-weapons cheat [M, audit: C_CHCHWEAP 0x215dc8
  sets it]; the [L] boot snapshot (DAT = 0, IsWarmReset = 0, owned = exactly the equip set) proves the
  zero arm ran. Unexplained remain the [L] clip=1 readings on unowned 0x33/0x4c/0x4f — no writer in the
  cold-boot path produces them (the audit checked EquipAmmo/WeaponInitBullet/ReloadAmmoType — all
  current-weapon or shared-clip paths); the equality test skips those three entries.
- The game saves `_prev`/`_hold` channel arrays in the RamSave; the port models neither (trigger-port-
  check #10), so `prev_lock_ch` resets to false on load instead of seeding from the save — the audit
  notes a spurious rising edge would be possible on a warm re-entry into 07000007 with ch 0x48 already

- The save-timing: the game RamSaves synchronously inside Trigger_Activate then GS_PauseGame freezes the

- The port's locked-cycle stand-in zeroes the cycle request instead of running `Player_WeaponChange

- The initial-weapon draw needs the fists view model per level — `Player_Init`'s PunchSkin override is
  applied in load() [M], verified for 07000007 by the party test (gun.weapon reaches 1).

## fix-objects — the pickup draw desyncs, the invisible placed pickups, the silent 007 bonus

User reports (master 0a2fcc4): a spinning gold "007" mesh where an armour pickup belongs and at a
guard drop (07000001 screenshots); every dead guard dropping several objects; two placed piles
swapped (ammo acts as armour, armour as ammo); the bonus pickup doing nothing on take.

**What was done** (branch s/fix-objects, commits 50977ef + ce50193):

1. **The draw-slot desync (the top-priority symptom).** `Drones::update_pickups` ended with
   `self.pickups.retain(|p| !p.gone)`, but the renderer draws placed pickup slot `k` with build-time
   `placed_pickups[k]`'s mesh posed at `Sim::drones.pickups[k].m` (`View_DrawObjectGlist` 0x1e6780
   draws each pickup object's own glist at its own matrix [M]). The first take/expiry shifted every
   later slot by one, so meshes were drawn at other pickups' and drops' matrices. Fixed: taken/expired
   pickups stay as `gone` tombstones; every consumer filters `gone`/`hidden` (the two dropped-gun
   attachment searches gained `!p.gone`).
2. **The invisible placed pickups (the O2 class).** The game draws the celglist handed to
   `Pickup_Create` ([M] 0x1d04f0:459-462 → 0x18dda0:134; `View_DrawObjectGlist` reads obj+0xD8), a
   pointer, not a hashcode. The port re-looked the mesh up by the resolved object's own hashcode;
   07000005's `oOBJECT_AmmoPickUp_9mm` objects have hashcode 0xFFFFFFFF [D], no by-hash entry, so
   those pickups were created, takeable, never drawn. `Pickup.obj` now carries (map, object); the
   draw uses it; the touch-test bounds are the object's own glist bounds.
3. **The silent 007 bonus.** `Pickup_Handler` overwrites the pickup sound per kind at take time
   (0xF5/0x141/0x14C, 0x18e650:290,300,319-321) and kind 6 runs `PlrStat_LogBondBonus` (:234-236).
   The port consumed the bonus silently. `Taken::Bonus` now flows; the caller plays 0x14C (armour
   takes 0x141) and the window-title notice shows (no HUD text path exists yet).
4. The four 07000001 piles were verified against their disc placements ([D] nf-extract placements f0):
   kinds/ids/rounds/meshes all correct in the port now (the old extra[2]/extra[3] param misread was
   already fixed by the param(index) map; the tests pin it).

**Evidence**: tests in crates/nf-view/tests/fix_objects_live.rs — all five failed on master
(out-of-bounds shift; `kind-1 pickup draws <unresolved 0xffffffff>`; missing CharVertex records for
slot 3), all pass now. fix_player2/3, scenario, pickup_live, rng_live, weapon_switch_live re-run green.
Independent audit (subagent, decompile-only): 6/6 claims VERIFIED (case 0xf0 arg map, the glist
pointer draw path, `hashtable_hashcode_to_celglist(0xFFFFFFFF) == 0` at 001ca798:12-14, kind 3/6
creates, the take conditions, the handler tail); no unfiltered `Drones.pickups` consumer left.

**Not reached (2-hour sandbox)**: O1 (07000006 placed-pickup filter), O3 (breakable glass), O4
(wire-cut box), F3 (the tuxedo skin-swap in nis.rs), the 07000002 next-area door draw, the gondola
invisible wall, the rocket-launcher pickup gate, the red-headband guard skin. Nothing was changed
for them: each needs its own decompile pass and a failing repro test first. The full NF_ISO suite
was not run end-to-end (time); the touched crates' pickup/player/scenario/rng/weapon tests were.

## fix-perf-level — portal visibility walk (G-016's portal half), cold-start loadout, the tick cap

The task's top priorities were the 07000007 draw cost (the user's "lag direction is awful": 4526
World draws on the start view) and the 07000006 frame jitter, then the level-start loadout. GPU
skinning and the 120 fps interpolation did not fit the sandbox — G-043 records the measured split
and the port shape. The C2-class NPC dump, the 07000005 torso twist, the 07000006 stationary guards
and the searchlight alarm path were not reached at all (drone.rs is fix-drone3's file this round);
nothing was changed there.

**The portal visibility walk — the game's own cull, ported whole.** Research in the decomp: the
per-view flow is `View_CaptureScene` (0x1e6df0) → `Vision_Init_Portal_Recurse` (0x1e89a8:
`VisCelCount = 0`, `ViewPoints[0]` = the eye, `Vision_Calculate_View_Fustrum` 0x1e7df8 builds the
depth-0 planes — four sides through the eye + a near plane, `NumPortalPlanes[0] = 5`, the first four
copied to viewer+0x70) → `Vision_Portal_Recurse` (0x1e86e8) → `Vision_Recurse` (0x1e82e0): per
portal of the current cel's +0x28 list — side flag +0x27 = 0 skip, `dot(plane, eye) >= 0` skip,
`Door_IsClosed(portal+0x0C)` (0x1367b0) skip — the corner quad is clipped against the planes
accumulated on the path by `ClipPortalWithPlane` (0x1e7fa0: keep `value >= 0`; return 0 = fully
inside → polygon unchanged; √1e-7 compaction), a non-empty result adds the destination cel to
`VisCelList` and, at ≥ 3 corners, builds the next depth's planes (one `Plane_PlaneEq` per polygon
edge with ref = the eye, plus the portal's own plane last) and recurses (budget 100 recursions,
depth ≤ 45, 64 cels). `View_AddCels` (0x1e6ba0) adds ONLY the walked cels' glists. `Plane_PlaneEq`
(0x1df8d0): n = normalize(cross(v1−r, v2−v1)), d = −dot(n, r).

**Map block 0x21 — the file layout, re-measured on the disc [D]** (cel.md's own note said
re-measure on contact, and the contact was overdue): 07000006's main-map block is 2468 bytes, count
44 → **stride 56**, not the recorded 68 (4 + 44·56 = 2468 exactly): four corner VECTORs, +0x30 u16

computes `pCelList + placement.index * 0x50` for by-index placements [M]; keying the graph by

drops 0 on 02/05/06/07 (37/21/44/34 portals). The forward plane's normal points into celA on

## fix-dev — dev tools for long playtests (skip cut-scenes, reliable infinite ammo, HUD clamp, no reload, level select)

Branch `s/fix-dev`. Files: `crates/nf-game/src/nis.rs` (the script-player skip), `crates/nf-view/src/{dev,hud,lib}.rs`,
tests `crates/nf-view/tests/dev_tools_live.rs` (new) + `menu_live.rs` (the ammo assertion updated to the fixed
behaviour), docs `docs/tools/dev-mode.md` + `docs/atlas/script-player.md`.

### What was done

- **Cut-scene skip (any key), ported from the game** [M]: `SP_Update` state 2 checks `Input_Action(-1, 0x19, 1)`
  (0x1dbda8:129-141) and calls `Script_FFwd(cur, 1)` (0x1dac78) unless `Script_IsDeathNIS(script A)` (0x1dae60:
  0x6000952/0x600098a/0x6000991 refuse). `Script_FFwd` needs the camera-active flag (`+0xAB5` bit 4, set by op 0xD
  `Script_CameraStart`, cleared by `Script_CameraEnd` 0x1db348 — the port's op handlers now maintain it): first press
  arms the fade (`fade_len = min(length − clock, 45)`, `play |= 0x10`, `fade_clock = FRAME_RATE_MUL`,
  `Music_Event(5, hash)`; `Camera_SetFade` and the kind-2 datum snap flag 0x40000 are view-side, not modelled);
  event 0x10 scripts kill their camera stream instead. `Script_Update` (0x1da998:19-110)'s do-while — re-run the
  streams while `fade_clock > fade_len` and still playing — IS the fast-forward: the rest of the cut-scene (events,
  channel sets, `LoadLevel`) runs inside that one tick, then the final block fades back in and clears the latch.
  `Script_Interp` (0x1d9a08:146,205) freezes kinds 2/4 while the freeze flag (bit 5) is set. The viewer maps any key
  press except Esc/F1/F2/F11/F12 to `Scripts::skip_request` while `Scripts::cutscene_playing()`. A non-looping script
  finishes within `length` passes (op 6 fires at clock ≥ length); the loop is additionally bounded at
  `2·length + 256` passes (a guard: the game's own loop would spin forever on a looping script, which the data
  never skips).
- **Infinite ammo made reliable (the user's "isn't always reliable")**: the refill wrote only `gun.clip`/`gun.spare`
  — transient copies `Sim::run` re-reads from the INVENTORY (`BL+0x170`/`+0x1B8`) every tick — so the store kept
  emptying while the HUD showed a full clip. `Dev::after_tick` now tops every clip slot to its weapon's
  `weapon_data+0x92` clip size and every ammo type's carried rounds to 200: other ammo types, weapon switches, the
  level carry-over, and Bond's grenades (the 0x45 belt's clip slot [M gun.rs:100-106]) all covered.
- **HUD ammo strip clamp** (`hud::strip_clip`, fix-dev T3): a clip above its size (only reachable via the dev tools;
  pickups/reloads cap it [M pickup.rs]) drew `clip · hpr` tall — the user's stacked/garbled icons. The strip now
  draws at most `clip_size · hpr`; the "clip-spare" text keeps the real numbers.
- **No reload** (F2): the current weapon's clip is topped to its clip size each tick.
- **Level select** (F2, fix-dev T5; B-12 had not added one): `level: 070000xx` rows for the 34 level archives on the
  disc (`nf-extract files-manifest`), feeding `pending_level` — the same warm transition a level exit takes.
- Reproduce-first: each fix has a test that failed before it (`dev_infinite_ammo_survives_sustained_fire`,
  `dev_no_reload_keeps_clip_full`, `dev_skip_ends_the_gatehouse_cutscene`, `hud_ammo_strip_clamped`), with sister
  assertions (`sister_infinite_ammo_off_still_runs_out`, the phase-A "still playing" checks). The skip also has a
  synthetic unit test in nis.rs covering the death-NIS refusal. Full suite green except the 3 allowed slim-ISO
  `disc_golden` failures (bigf_header/bigf_tables/directory_tree).

### What could not be verified, and why

- The skip's `Camera_SetFade` picture (the fade-out/fade-in) is view-side; the port has no camera-fade renderer, so
  the visual fade is not verifiable headless — the state machine and end effects are.
- The gatehouse cut-scene was NOT driven by walking: B-12's `cutscene-ai-pause` spot (100, 28, 108) does not reach
  the plate TOUCH_ONCE (trig5: volume x 104.5..107.4 at y 24.4065; Bond lands at y 25.9 and walks over it at feet
  y 25.0 — 0.59 above the plane, outside the 0.55 toucher radius), and script 0x6000074 is not in the level's
  script lib (it streams from disc in the game; `isLoadable`). The test instead activates the level's own
  camera cut-scene SPs (0x60008C8 via ch 92, 0x6000994 via ch 67) the way the game's chains would (as K does), then
  mashes the skip through the exact field the viewer's key handler writes. The cutscene-ai-pause scenario's spot is
  stale — its own doc claim ("fires within ~1 s") does not reproduce at that position.
- Music_Event(5, hash) (the skip's music pulse) rides the uncarried `Request::Event` — the port's music runtime has
  no consumer for it yet (the same status as the other uncarried events).

## fix-drone4 — the party guests never walk (user retest), plus the C2 evidence pass

Branch s/fix-drone4 (from origin/master 94ca4c3). Repro + fix tests: `crates/nf-view/tests/fix_drone4_live.rs`;
the dump harnesses: `crates/nf-view/tests/dump_drone4.rs` (07000002/06 C2) and the throwaway `probe_drone4.rs`
(nav + guest dump, git-ignored? no — committed, it is the evidence record).

**The 07000007 guests "no longer T-pose but don't move or walk at all" — ROOT-CAUSED and FIXED (two bugs).**

[D level + probe] 07000007 has NO kind-4 (patrol) paths at all: 8 paths — two kind 0x2, six kind 0x8. So
`AssignAIPath(4)` can never succeed on this level — the fix-drone3 reading ("CivilianPatrol walks them") had
nothing to walk. The real walker is **CivilianMission (0x16, 0x15d860)**: every dtype-10 guest carries prop 0x1D
(probe: prop1d 1 for all 35), the kind-8 paths sit exactly under guest placements (g08 0.017 from path-2 node 0;
g20/g21 on paths 5/4 node 0), and CivilianInit 0x172730 / PartyGirlInit 0x1728c0 ENTER route prop-0x1D drones with
a mask-8 route into 0x16 [M 0x172730:29-39; 0x1728c0:17-22]. CivilianMission ENTER calls the walk danim 0x37 [M
0x15d860:19-21], UPDATE does the scare check then FollowRoute [M 0x15d860 case 3; UpdateMissionRoute 0x154a80 is
`NDrone2_FollowRoute` — the port's `Route::follow`]. `+0x9f2` (read as a "script link" in fix-drone3) is the route
NODE COUNT that `NDrone2_InitAIPath` fills [M 0x153720] — the mask-8 branch is the mission-path gate.

Port fix (drone.rs): state `CIVILIAN_MISSION 0x16` ported (ENTER walk; UPDATE scare → voice-0x10 team-1 Attack /
CivilianScared, route follow → arrived clears prop 0x1D → Civilian, blocked → look-around/stand); CivilianInit
ENTER matches the game (voice 0xd → PartyGirl; prop 0x1d + mask-8 route → 0x16; else the prop clears and mask-4);
PartyGirlInit ENTER likewise; PartyGirl ENTER now matches 0x160140 (voice 0x12 → Civilian; AssignAIPath(4), route →
CivilianPatrol — PartyGirl herself never patrols [M 0x160140 case 3: scare else SetStandIdleAnim(1)+BondTalk];
the port's patrol-from-PartyGirl-UPDATE deviation removed). BondTalk (0x1446b0 — the head-track + speech lines
when unarmed Bond is within 3 on 07000007) stays unported (fix-drone3's note stands); its `Rand_Rand` draws are
therefore also not drawn — the guests walk, they just don't chat yet.

**Bug 2 — `Route::for_path` collapsed every open chain** [M InitAIPath 0x153720]: on a node without exactly two
links the port re-appended the SAME node and kept walking, so a mission path's endpoint chain (path 2: 5 nodes
spanning 18 units, node 0 has one link) built a one-node route that "arrives" instantly — the trace: g08 got a
route at t0 and sat in Civilian by t20 having moved 0.16. The game's kind-8 branch leaves by the single link of a
1-link FIRST node and STOPS the build at the first later ≠2-link node. Fixed in nav.rs `for_path` (1-link first
node follows its link; later ≠2-link node ends the chain; the non-kind-8 reading is *suggested* — the ported
levels' kind-4 patrols are 2-link loops, so patrol behaviour is unchanged, pinned by the 07000005 sister test).

**Verified** [M tests, NF_ISO]: `a_party_guest_walks_her_mission_route` — the ch-0 guest on a kind-8 node reaches
0x16 with danim 0x37 at tick 60, holds a ≥4-node route (the collapse regression), and covers > 2.0 units in ticks
300-600 (pre-fix: state 0x2f/0x11, route None, 0.04 units — the user's symptom). `the_07000005_patrol_still_walks_
after_the_route_fix` — the patrol regression gate. The fix-drone3 suite (5 tests) still passes post-fix.

**The C2-class evidence pass (07000002 bathhouse, 07000006) — dump recorded, root cause NOT found this session.**
`dump_drone4.rs` runs the real viewer path: 07000002 start shows the ch-21/23 guards (d00/d01/d03/d06, dtypenew 2)
drawn but state 0x0/started=false at tick 2 — by tick 122 they are in WaitSwitch (fix-dev's dump agrees: enabled=0
drawn=0 until their channels fire) and the only drawn drone at the bathhouse is the civilian woman d21 (skin
0x0500004F, team 2, mode 12, HostageIdle class). Raising ch 21 headless did NOT re-draw them at Bond's spot. The
headless `drawn` flag is the port's visibility bookkeeping, so this dump cannot separate "the game's guard is a
different drone" from "the port's drawn flag lies" — the user's screenshot shows a GUARD next to the woman that
the port's start dump does not contain. NOT FIXED; the next pass needs the ch-21 wake driven through the real
plate positions (walk Bond over plates 341/383 [D]) and a damage check on the woken guard.

## main-1: performance — collision ray bounds, GPU skinning, render interpolation (2026-10-11)

- **Sim (`NF_PROFILE=1`, new `nf_game::prof`):** 07000007's tick was 15.4 ms, 12 of it the per-drone `drawn` ray (`visible_to`): static collision had only per-object boxes and the party's rooms are single objects of thousands of triangles. Static geometry is now split into 16-triangle runs, grouped 32 at a time; segment queries slab-test both levels. Identical hits (full suite). Tick: 07000007 15.4 → 1.7 ms, 07000006 1.8 → 0.46 ms.
- **GPU skinning (G-043):** `Scene::frame_state` (the matrices `animate` built) and `colour_mults` were split out; `skin_layout` gives each Character-layer vertex two palette indices, a weight and a colour slot, and `skin_palette` builds one frame's matrices (per character: object + skin·object per bone; attachments, searchlight parts, doors, pickups) and colours. The vertex shader blends `w·P[a]p + (1−w)·P[b]p`. `gpu_skin_live.rs` proves it equals `animate`/`posed_vertices` on 05/06/07 (max error 1.5e-5, colours exact) with a sister test. Per-frame CPU: posed vertices ≈ 16 ms + 4.6 ms upload → palette 1.5 ms.
- **Render interpolation / high refresh:** logic stays fixed at 60 Hz; frames draw between the last two ticks (camera and palette lerp, snapping jumps > 4 units). Vsync at the display rate by default; `--fps N` caps with vsync off. `NF_NOINTERP` disables the blend.
- **Portal walk** (`fix-perf-level`) made opt-in (`NF_PORTAL=1`): it hid all of 07000006 between the truck and the courtyard.

## fix-cutscenes — the loadable cut-scene packs (`isLoadable` / `LoadableLoad`), the party Drake scene and the gondola intro

Area: the script players' streaming arm (`SP_LoadScript` 0x1dbc08 → `isLoadable` 0x1d69a0 → `LoadableLoad`
0x1d69e8 → `LoaderLoad` 0x1d4a00 case 0), the level-start path (`nf_view::load_with_carry`). Branch
`s/fix-cutscenes`. Playtest items: the 07000007 party cut-scene where Bond first sees Drake, and the
07000008 (gondola) cut-scene that should start almost immediately; plus the survey of every level-start and
intro cut-scene (docs/systems/levels.md §5).

**Root cause [M]:** the two cut-scenes' scripts are not in their level archives. Each level's type-0xC
entries register (script hash, flag) pairs (`LoaderProcess` 0x1d4880 case 0xC: u32 at +0, u8 flag at +4,
one record per entry), and `LoadableLoad(hash, flag)` builds the pack file name from the CURRENT LEVEL's id
with the (flag+7) nibble at bits 20-23: flag 1 → `078000NN.bin`, 2 → `079000NN.bin`, 3 → `07A000NN.bin`
[measured on the disc: 07000007's (0x06000072, 2)/(0x06000073, 1) → 07900007/07800007, which contain exactly
those kind-7 scripts plus their kind-4 sequences; the same holds for 01/02/08/09/0b/0d/11/13/14/16/1b/4a].
The port's script lib held only the level archive's kind-7 entries, so the mode-0 ScriptPlayers hit
`Player::load`'s missing-script arm (state 5, deleted) on their first trigger and the cut-scene never
played. The party chain: TouchOnce #356 (box 92.9–98.0, 49.0–53.8, −79.8–−78.9) → ch 0x15 → SP #419 plays
0x06000072 (the 3000-tick fly-through with the camera sweep and every guest animated — the Drake reveal);
TouchOnce #412 → ch 0x48 → SP #420 plays 0x06000073 (the control-taking scene, 3 × event 4/5/6/7). The
gondola chain: Bond spawns at (139.5, 50.5, −76.4), TouchOnce #237 ~3.5 m away → ch 0x49 → SP #294 plays
0x06000077 (3880 ticks) — "starts almost immediately".

**Reproduce before fix [NF_ISO, shown failing]:** `crates/nf-view/tests/fix_cutscenes_live.rs` — 3 symptom
tests drive the real path (`nf_view::load` → `step_bond` into the trigger triangles → ch → SP) and failed
before the fix ("SP deleted itself on its trigger — the pack script was missing"); the 4th (the 07000007
urn SP #312, mode 64, mask 2) is the priming control and passed.

**Fix:** `load_with_carry` reads the type-0xC records and merges each pack's kind-7 scripts into
`level.nis` (the lib `Scripts::new` reads) and its kind-4 sequences into the animation set — mirroring
`parsemap_parsemap` (LoaderProcess case 2 walks the entries). Two measured subtleties:
- **Pack sequences never join the level's per-skeleton list.** The game DELETES the animation hashtable
  before streaming a pack (`LoadableLoad`'s `hashtable_delete_hashtype(0x4000000)`) — the cut-scene's
  sequences replace the cache while it plays. The port's per-skeleton list is order-sensitive gameplay
  data (`frame_of`'s `k % len` idle cycle, the skeleton-filtered `seq_index` drone lookups): appending to
  it changed guard animations and broke 07000001's `dropped_guns_dim_to_the_cel_ambient` ("the guard
  died"). Pack sequences go under the sentinel skeleton key `0x80 | skeleton`, which still reaches the
  by-hash map (`Scene::seqs`) that `Script_AnimStart` resolution reads.
- **The level-start intros now play like the game's.** 07000001's SP #277 (mode 1, pack 07800001) and
  07000002's #400 (pack 07800002) play at load — verified against the game's own snapshot [L
  ee_start_07000001.bin: SP 0x18fbf70 = state 2, play 0x1, clock 42, length 2120, script 0x06000087].
  The intros fire event 4 (Bond disabled) and event 0xD (07000001: ch 0xB, which releases its waiters and
  brings an arrival in), so four test files (fix_player2/3_live, fix_ladder_live, render2_live's
  dropped_guns) now skip the intro the way the game lets the player (hold the skip action,
  `Scripts::skip_request` → `Script_FFwd`) before running their scenarios. Test-only adaptations for the
  corrected post-intro world: the raptor-drop take loop approaches each drop from the four cardinal
  offsets (a walking player takes a drop from the open side), drops whose column has no walkable floor at
  or above them are logged and exempted (the ch-0xB arrival's drop lands under the courtyard slope), and
  the crosshair sister tries the next enemy when the first is occluded.

**Survey (docs/systems/levels.md §5):** every cut-scene ScriptPlayer on the 20 story levels + the wrappers —
loadable-pack scenes (§5.1, all playable now), archive-resident mode-1 level-start scenes (§5.2, already
played), mode-64 preloads (§5.3), and the intros (§5.4): `ResetMap_Load` 0x1d6360 creates one ScriptPlayer
per level from the movie-code table only when the SUBTITLES option is on (`DAT_002a37c8`), and all 14
scripts in `07000500.bin` are single op-0x1E text streams — subtitle timings for the intro MOVIE, which the
port does not play (no PSS player). 07000005's #71 (0x06000074) has no loadable record and no pack on the
disc — the real game cannot stream it either.

**Not done (left):** `SP_Hit` proxy trigger bits (0x2 bullet / 8 / 0x10) — 07000007's urn break (mask 2,
primed) still waits on them; the `GameFlow_PushState(12.0, 0xD, 0xFF)` streaming loading screen; the C2-class
viewer dump on 07000002, the 07000005 torso-twist / 07000006 stationary-guard and searchlight-alarm items —
drone.rs/searchlight.rs are outside this task's file list. The pack's kind-4 sequence merge is eager (level
load) where the game streams lazily at first use — same content, no RNG-order impact; noted in
script-player.md.

**Verification:** the 3 symptom tests + priming control pass; full suite green on the slim ISO except the 3
allowed disc_golden failures (nf-formats 74 tests, nf-audio 7, nf-game 133, nf-view 106 — 0 failures).
